kurzfassung: Composting food waste significantly reduces greenhouse gas emissions and returns vital nutrients to the soil. Various methods exist for different living situations, ranging from municipal pickup and backyard piles to apartment box methods and commercial services. Choosing the right kitchen container, properly managing odors, and understanding what materials can actually break down are key to success.
stichpunkte: Food waste in landfills produces methane, making composting a powerful individual climate action.
Composting options range from local drop-offs and commercial pickup services to backyard bins and apartment box methods.
A successful compost pile requires a balanced mix of nitrogen-rich greens and carbon-rich browns.
Home composting setups generally cannot reach the high temperatures needed to break down bioplastics and compostable cutlery.
Everyday items like stainless steel mixing bowls work better for collecting scraps than specialized compost bins.
Freezing food scraps is an effective way to eliminate kitchen odors and save counter space between drop-offs.
Countertop electric devices dehydrate food scraps into smaller volumes, but they do not produce true compost.
Regular maintenance, such as washing bins with a vinegar-water solution and letting them dry, prevents foul odors.

clips.hook: Why food waste in landfills harms the planet
clips.text: Decomposing food in landfills generates methane gas, and discarded food constitutes the largest material category in American solid waste streams.

clips.hook: Composting inside an apartment without smells
clips.text: Apartment dwellers can maintain a slow-breakdown box method using dry organic materials that remains completely odorless with frequent mixing.

clips.hook: Why compostable forks don't break down at home
clips.text: Small backyard setups lack the sustained high temperatures of industrial facilities, meaning bioplastic cutlery and bags will not decompose properly.

clips.hook: How composting actually reduces kitchen smells
clips.text: Removing decomposing organic material from indoor trash cans and placing it into dedicated bins prevents foul odors from lingering in the kitchen.

clips.hook: The truth about expensive countertop food recyclers
clips.text: Electronic dehydrators reduce trash volume and create dry material, but they are expensive, prone to breaking, and do not produce actual compost.

beschreibung:
Before you dump your veggie peels and coffee grounds into the trash, consider the many reasons to compost. Keeping food waste out of landfills reduces greenhouse gas emissions, while nutrient-rich compost helps sequester carbon and rejuvenates soil. You’ll also likely need to empty your regular trash less frequently. For many people, the biggest barrier to composting is simply getting started.

In this episode, Wirecutter sustainability editor Katie Okamoto shares practical tips for collecting kitchen food scraps, navigating composting options without municipal pickup, and understanding what actually belongs in your bin—including why you might want to skip those biodegradable liner bags.

Plus, Wirecutter staff members break down their own real-world setups. They share how to manage commercial pickup services, why "compostable" plastics don't work in backyard bins, and strategies for keeping odors at bay.

This episode covers:
Composting options for every space: If you don't have municipal green-bin pickup, you can use private commercial services, drop off scraps at community gardens or farmer's markets, or even try the "cardboard box method" to compost slowly inside your home.
Backyard composting 101: A successful pile requires a balance of "greens" (fresh food waste) and "browns" (dry leaves, paper, or cardboard).
Strategies for collecting food scraps: You don't need a specialized bin. Wide-mouthed mixing bowls or restaurant Cambro bins work well.
The freezer scrap method: Keeping a squishable storage bag in your freezer to collect veggie peels and eggshells eliminates odors, saves counter space, and makes it easy to tote scraps to a drop-off site.
